topics.label: Oceans
facts: Oceans cover about 70 percent of Earth's surface.
There are five oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.
Ocean water is salty, and the salt comes from rocks and minerals washed into the sea.

questions.q: About how much of Earth's surface is covered by oceans?
questions.fact: Oceans cover roughly 70 out of every 100 parts of Earth's surface.
The Pacific is the biggest ocean, larger than all Earth's land put together.

choices: Salt from rocks is washed into the sea
questions.fact: Rivers carry tiny amounts of salt from rocks into the sea, where it builds up.

questions.q: How many oceans are there on Earth?
questions.fact: The five oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic.

topics.label: Magnets
facts: A magnet pulls some metals towards it, especially iron, nickel, and cobalt.
Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole.
Opposite poles attract each other, and like poles push each other away.
Earth itself acts like a giant magnet, which is why compass needles point north.

questions.q: Which metal does a magnet pull strongly?
questions.fact: Magnets pull iron, nickel, and cobalt most strongly.

questions.q: What happens when two north poles are pushed together?
questions.fact: Like poles repel each other, while opposite poles attract.

questions.q: What are the two ends of a magnet called?
choices: The north pole and the south pole
questions.fact: Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole.

questions.q: Why does a compass needle point north?
choices: Earth acts like a giant magnet
questions.fact: Earth's magnetic field pulls the compass needle towards the magnetic north.

topics.label: Simple Machines
facts: Simple machines are tools that make work easier, like levers, pulleys, wheels, and ramps.
A lever is a bar that turns on a fixed point called a fulcrum.
A wheel and axle lets things roll instead of sliding, which takes much less effort.
A ramp, or inclined plane, lets you move heavy things up slowly instead of lifting them straight up.

questions.q: Which of these is a simple machine?
questions.fact: Levers, pulleys, wheels and axles, ramps, screws, and wedges are simple machines.

questions.q: What is the fixed point a lever turns on called?
questions.fact: A lever turns on its fulcrum, like a seesaw turning on its middle point.

choices: It lets things roll instead of sliding
questions.fact: Rolling takes much less effort than dragging something along the ground.

questions.q: What does a ramp help you do?
choices: Move heavy things up more easily
questions.fact: A ramp lets you push a heavy load up slowly instead of lifting it all at once.

topics.label: Rivers and Lakes
facts: A river is water that flows across land, usually starting in hills or mountains and ending in a sea or ocean.
A lake is a large area of still water surrounded by land.
The Amazon River carries more water than any other river in the world.
Many animals and plants depend on rivers and lakes for drinking water, food, and a place to live.

questions.q: Where does a river usually end?
choices: In a desert with no water
questions.fact: Rivers flow downhill until they reach a sea, an ocean, or a lake.

choices: A large area of still water surrounded by land
questions.fact: A lake is a large body of water that is surrounded by land.

questions.q: Which river carries more water than any other?
questions.fact: The Amazon carries more water than any other river on Earth.

questions.q: Why are rivers and lakes important for wildlife?
choices: They give animals drinking water, food, and homes
questions.fact: Rivers and lakes provide water, food, and habitats for many living things.
